clue.text: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign

definitions.text: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign

parts.words: Hewas always ready to accept a new sovereign
parts.note: describes the turncoat cleric of the old song, who kept his parish by switching loyalty to each new king or queen

explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is the hero of an 18th-century English song who changed his religion under every monarch from Charles II to George I to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's clergyman is proverbial for trimming his beliefs to suit whichever ruler took the throne.

clue.text: Character missing from the Irish flag

indicators.note: something missing from a word is dropped out of its letters

parts.note: the Irish as a people is IRISH
a character is a letter of the alphabet, here the H

explanation.surface: A symbol or letter has been left off Ireland's national banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner here but the wild yellow flag, a plant of the iris family.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is the common name for wild irises growing by water.

clue.text: Bird comes up to other birds

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that comes up is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: One bird flies up to join a group of others.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots, a different family from the skua.

clue.text: They're not at home with regulations

definitions.text: They're not at home with regulations

parts.note: someone not at home is out
regulations are laws

explanation.surface: People who feel uncomfortable with rules and red tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlaws are fugitives living beyond the protection and rules of society.

clue.text: British Rail gets directions on how to make tea

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former national railway
E and W are the compass directions east and west

explanation.surface: The railway company issues instructions on preparing a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail was the UK's nationalised railway, famous for its buffet tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew is to steep leaves in hot water to prepare a pot of tea.

clue.text: Where you may buy duty-free wine on display

indicators.note: on here sets the wine after the word for display, so it follows on from it

parts.note: to air something is to display it publicly
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A tax-free shop where wine is set out for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free shops sit in the departure lounges of terminals for international flights.

clue.text: Band-leader waves at cus tomers

indicators.note: the letters wave about, moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bandleader acknowledges the crowd with a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' is not a musical group here but a troop of Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: A scout troop is a band of boys, and its adult leader holds that title.

clue.text: Don't get confused when you notice you have a good hand

parts.note: to notice is to see
a straight, five cards in sequence, is a strong poker hand

explanation.surface: A card player keeps a clear head on spotting a winning deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To think and perceive clearly, without muddle, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Port area

definitions.meaning: A historic harbour town in northern Israel
a unit of land measure, 4,840 square yards

explanation.definitionFit: Acre is both a Mediterranean harbour city and a measure of land surface.

clue.text: Shriek at cat when upset and despondent

indicators.note: the letters are upset, knocked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone screams at the cat when distressed and miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being heartsick means deeply unhappy or dejected.

clue.text: He may be booted on the stage

definitions.text: He may be booted on the stage

parts.words: He may be booted on the stage
parts.note: points to the pantomime cat who wears boots, rather than an actor kicked off

explanation.walkthrough: Puss in Boots is a staple British Christmas pantomime; 'booted' suggests being thrown out but means wearing boots.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat hero of the fairy tale is a familiar stage character in panto.

clue.text: Tied sort of worker?

parts.note: a worker who is tied means one wearing a necktie, an office employee, not one bound

explanation.definitionFit: Office and clerical staff are classed by the shirt and tie they traditionally wear.

clue.text: Neat and precise form of epitaph

indicators.note: a form of the words gives them a new shape

explanation.surface: Tidy, exact wording for a gravestone inscription.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase RIP is the commonest inscription on a tombstone.

clue.text: One who'd change for the dance

explanation.surface: Someone who would get changed before going to the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American country square dance or the party where it happens.

clue.text: Inter alia find saltpetre

indicators.note: Latin for other things, read as telling us to make something other of the letters

explanation.surface: Among other things, one comes across potassium nitrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter alia' reads as the Latin tag for 'among other things'; split, 'alia' asks for INTER in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, also spelt niter in the US.

clue.text: Shemakeshatsmoredecorative yetneater

definitions.meaning: the clue's run-together words read as She makes hats more decorative: a milliner who adds ribbons and ornaments
the run-together words read yet neater: more tidy, comparative of trim

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has lost its spaces: it reads She makes hats more decorative yet neater, two definitions joined by 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat trimmer adds the finishing ornaments, and trimmer also means tidier.

clue.text: Heath Robinson's heart beat

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase is its inner letters running across the two names

explanation.surface: The cartoonist's pulse quickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist known for drawing absurdly complicated machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong rhythmic pulse, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: It's to be seen on a rifle

definitions.meaning: the aiming device fitted to a gun barrel

explanation.definitionFit: A sight is both a thing worth viewing and a gun's aiming aid.

clue.text: Drinks to the return of a good man

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a return sends the abbreviation back the other way

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A toast to a righteous fellow coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tots are small measures of spirits.

clue.text: A way one takes wine

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a glass of wine along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Former churchman?

definitions.meaning: the head of a priory, a monastic house

explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier, and a monastic superior ranks just below an abbot.

clue.text: Locate unpleasant smell, but this won't cure it

parts.note: to locate something is to place it
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Find the source of a nasty pong, though this remedy will not fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill has no active medical ingredient and heals nothing itself.

clue.text: Refreshed sheep tear about

indicators.note: the word for tear goes about, around, the sheep

parts.note: to rend is to tear
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A revived sheep rips around the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Something renewed has been restored or made fresh again.

clue.text: Sympathise with number drawing unemployment benefit

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
someone drawing benefit is on the dole, British slang for unemployment pay

explanation.surface: Feeling for a numbered claimant collecting jobless pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dole' is British slang for state unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To condole is to express sorrow for another's loss.

clue.text: Beg for quarter in the wood

indicators.note: the quarter sits in the middle of the tree name

parts.note: beech is a hardwood tree
SE, southeast, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Pleading for mercy while lost among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or plead earnestly.

clue.text: Right out of line

indicators.note: the letters are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A correct position that has broken ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: A girl raised a cry of woe

indicators.note: in a down clue a raised word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: Sal is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman lifts her voice in lament.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret.

clue.text: A drop in rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye when crying
a rip or split in cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt alike, one sense is a teardrop and the other a rip.

clue.text: Labour staged a walk-out?

definitions.meaning: the UK Labour Party is on the political ...

explanation.definitionFit: The left wing of politics, and the past tense of leave.

clue.text: Tropical disease that may make one feel very low

indicators.note: the words are made into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: An illness of hot countries that leaves sufferers depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito-borne viral infection of Africa and South America causing jaundice.

clue.text: A way through on foot

definitions.meaning: a curved opening one passes under
the raised curve of the sole

explanation.definitionFit: An archway is a passage, and the foot has a curved instep.

clue.text: Thoughtful enough to study the team and make an assessment

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a side is a team
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: A careful manager studies the squad before judging it.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerate means caring about others' feelings.
